note: baseline measurement on one machine with server and clients on loopback; not a capacity promise

workload.server: separate process, ThreadingHTTPServer + SQLite WAL synchronous=FULL
workload.durability: every batch is one committed transaction (fsync) before its ack

interpretation: All 120000 deliveries were acknowledged with zero errors and the database holds exactly 100000 unique events and 20000 logged duplicates. The latency tail (p95 ~12.6 s) is queueing: 100 concurrent clients contend for SQLite's single writer and each batch is an fsync'd transaction. Server peak RSS (~650 MB) is dominated by 100 concurrent handler threads each holding a thread-local SQLite connection. Both are first-version baselines on one 8-core 8 GB laptop with clients on loopback, not production targets; the PostgreSQL port and a bounded worker pool are the documented next steps if a tighter p95 is required.
